results.summary: This design generates a pulse-width modulated (PWM) waveform with a duty cycle set by a 7-bit input. An internal counter is compared against the duty cycle value to produce a high output while the counter is below the threshold. Testing requires a clock signal and an oscilloscope or logic analyzer to observe the output waveform. The design is a straightforward PWM generator with no external hardware beyond measurement equipment.

This asynchronous FIFO enables data transfer between two clock domains using separate read and write clocks. It uses Gray-coded pointers for synchronization and provides full and empty flags. The design can be fully simulated without external hardware, but on an FPGA, LEDs or UART may be used to display status. It is a standard implementation of a clock-domain-crossing FIFO.

This design implements a multiply-accumulate (MAC) unit for 2x2 matrix multiplication with 4-bit operands, intended for neural network applications. It includes control signals for write, read, clear, and accumulation enable. Testing involves providing matrices and observing the output, which is read in two 8-bit parts. The design is inspired by existing matrix-MAC units and requires a personal computer for control.

This design is a digital simplification of a leaky integrate-and-fire neuron, which accumulates input current until a threshold is reached, then emits a pulse. It requires an external ADALM2000 to provide a constant DC input voltage, and the output is observed via an LED. The design operates at a low clock frequency of 20 kHz and is a demonstration of a biological neuron model for neural networks.

This programmable threshold voltage comparator compares an external reference voltage with one of eight selectable threshold levels, seven fixed and one user-defined. It uses a resistor ladder and passgates controlled by a decoder, and outputs a digital high when the reference exceeds the threshold. Testing requires a 1.8V supply and input voltages up to 1.8V, with a maximum switching frequency of 100 kHz. The design is analog-intensive and provides a flexible voltage sensing capability.

This project is an empty placeholder intended to pass DRC checks, with no functional documentation. The title suggests an ADC/DAC with an address ALU, but the description is nonsensical and provides no useful information. There is no indication of how the design works or how to test it. The documentation is insufficient to determine any actual functionality.

This is an all-digital phase-locked loop (PLL) implemented in RTL, operating at 2 MHz with a 50 MHz sampling clock and programmable parameters. It includes a digitally controlled oscillator (DCO) and provides outputs for lock detection and sign. Testing involves stepping the frequency and measuring lock time and jitter, requiring a function generator, oscilloscope, and external VCO. The design is notable for being fully digital and programmable.

This design implements a 9-to-4 priority encoder with a parity checker and a 7-segment display output. It supports selectable MSB or LSB priority and even or odd parity modes via input pins. The encoded value and parity bit are displayed on the 7-segment display, with the parity bit controlling the decimal point. Testing involves setting the mode pins and observing the outputs on the display and output pins.

This analog design biases an inverter for linear mode operation to act as an amplifier, with a multiplexer selecting parallel feedback resistors to change the gain. It requires an external 20 nF capacitor at the input and an oscilloscope to observe the output. Silicon tests show it works, with different output levels for each MUX setting. The design demonstrates a mixed-signal amplifier with programmable gain.

This project implements current-switching DACs for generating analog VGA signals, using a 16x16 matrix of unit current sources to convert 8-bit digital inputs to analog current outputs. It is intended for analog VGA displays and requires external pull-up resistors and opamps to convert the current to voltage. The digital display controller is not yet implemented, and testing details are incomplete. The design is an experiment in analog VGA signal generation.
